desc: Implement deterministic Miller-Rabin for 64-bit integers using bases [2, 325, 9375, 28178, 450775, 9780504, 1795265022].
Implement factor function for numbers up to 10^9 (trial division up to sqrt).
Implement get_prime_factors that factors k*N using known factors of N and trial division for small k.
Implement find_primitive_root that tries g=2,3,4,... until g^((p-1)/q) != 1 for all prime factors q of p-1.
Handle special cases: N=1 -> output (2,1); N<=60 -> output (2, 2^N-1).
For N>60: factor N, then loop k (stepping by 2 if N odd) to find prime p=kN+1, find primitive root g, compute A=g^((p-1)//N) mod p, output (A, p).
Run the solution on the sample input (4 test cases: 3, 16, 1, 55) and verify it produces correct output or valid solutions.
Verify the solution for N=16 produces a valid pair (A, M) with order exactly 16.
Verify the solution for N=55 produces a valid pair (A, M) with order exactly 55.
Check that A and M are within [1, 10^18] for all test cases.
Test with larger values of N (e.g., N=10^6, N=10^9) to ensure performance and correctness.
Optimize if necessary (e.g., improve factoring of k when k is large).
